name: Ollama Pro

reset.rule: Resets on the day of the month your subscription started, on monthly and annual plans.
stipulations: Usage is the dollar value of the tokens you use, at each model's per-token rate. Some models have cheaper cached-input and off-peak rates.
Unused credit is lost at the reset.
Switching plans resets usage, but the reset day stays on your original start date.
Usage data can lag behind your requests.

overage: Included credit is spent first, then purchased credit. Any plan can buy credit. Ollama's pricing post says you can keep going at the same per-token rate, but the Max page still calls extra usage "coming". Ollama doesn't say what happens with no purchased credit.

how: $60 of cloud model usage a month, counted at each model's per-token rate.
No 5-hour or weekly limit on the current plan. The month is the only window.
Up to 3 requests at once. Extra requests queue, and are rejected when the queue is full.
ext: Open models from other labs, priced per token: gpt-oss, DeepSeek V4, Kimi K3, GLM-5.x, MiniMax, Nemotron, Gemma 4 and more. The full list is at ollama.com/search?c=cloud.
Claude Code: run "ollama launch claude", or set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://ollama.com, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN to your Ollama API key and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to empty.
Ollama has official setup pages for Codex CLI, OpenCode and Cline.
quirks: Subscribers from before 31 Aug 2026 who keep auto-renewing stay on the old plan, with GPU-time 5-hour and weekly limits. Changing tier or billing cycle, or resubscribing, moves you to credits.
Cloud models don't support structured outputs.
In Claude Code, hosted web search and advanced tool controls aren't fully supported. Claude settings files can override the env vars, so check /status.
Ollama recommends a context length of 64k or more for larger repositories.
Cloud models can be retired. See the model lifecycle page.
GET ollama.com/api/usage reports dollars and tokens but no percentage or reset time. GET ollama.com/api/balance shows remaining credit.
Pro adds "larger Pro models", but Ollama doesn't list which ones.
